brief: Mixed US/Iran headlines (Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal but talks continue; Saudi restored its oil pipeline to half capacity) left WTI only modestly higher, so equity weakness was driven instead by a bond selloff: 2/5/10/30y yields rose 6-7bp, with the 10y hitting 5.25% intraday, a 19-year high, as hawkish Fedspeak (Cook said AI buildout can be inflationary; Barkin said AI isn't immune to rate pressure) combined with a hot Dallas Fed Mfg print. SPX fell 0.8%, tech lagged except NVDA (+1.3%) on an incremental $150bn buyback. META fell 5% for a second straight day even as it launched Meta Enterprise Platform and hired away MongoDB's CEO; the launch dragged enterprise software (HUBS, ADBE, CRM, NOW) and Muse-linked CPU names (INTC, AMD, ARM) lower on profit-taking and de-risking. JPM's US Market Intelligence desk moved back to Tactically Bullish from its Aug 31 Cautious/Neutral call, arguing yields will stabilize (Barry sees 10y at 5.05% by year-end) and oil trends lower; it drops the NDX/RTY pairing on squeeze risk, favoring Tech outright plus Banks ex-AI. Also previews JOLTS (openings seen rising to 7.40mn) and MU earnings, where Sur expects a beat on DRAM/NAND ASP strength.
